title: Meta and Microsoft's AI spending: a tale of two earnings reports
excerpt: The difference between the two is clear: AI spending is fine … as long as there is a direct and measurable return.
content_html:
Meta's message to investors: The AI spending will continue until returns improve.

Investors' response: No thanks.

AI spend was the big focus during Meta's Q2 earnings report. And the pitch wasn't convincing enough to stop an after-hours selloff.

Meta was happy to credit AI with helping its advertising business (its bread and butter) rise 27%. And it wasn't just pure growth. Ad impressions grew 14%, while the average price per ad climbed 12%.

There's just one catch. Meta is still spending an incredible amount — $31.1 billion, roughly double what it spent last year — on its AI bets. That's eating up a significant portion of its free cash flow, which went from $8.55 BILLION to $784 MILLION. One analyst said the AI strategy is like "throwing spaghetti at the wall."

Investors were unimpressed, with Meta's stock falling nearly 10% at one point after the bell.

Compare that to another tech giant that reported yesterday: Microsoft. It logged wins in Azure and Microsoft 365 Copilot, which Microsoft CFO Amy Hood touted in her quarterly memo to employees viewed by BI's Ashley Stewart. Perhaps more importantly, its AI budget forecast didn't budge.

Investors noticed. Microsoft's stock jumped almost 8% in after-hours trading.

The difference between the two is clear: AI spending is fine … as long as there is a direct and measurable return.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg made the case for why Meta's AI bets might need more time.

A lot of the most immediate use cases for AI are for developers. Just look at the boom in vibe coding. "Building for consumers is a little bit different," Zuckerberg said during Wednesday's earnings call, but it's also a "massive market opportunity."

And who better to serve that market than the king of all social networks? Between Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads, Meta has billions of users across its platforms. Zuckerberg said Meta's making a big bet on AI agents.

That all tracks with one small exception: A lot of Americans are really nervous about AI.

Meta has tried to ease those fears with a big AI PR push, including a Zuckerberg op-ed and some interviews with reporters. (The request to speak to BI Today must have got caught in my spam inbox. I'm happy to chat, Mark. Sounds like you have a really cool gym.)

BI's Peter Kafka has an idea about how Meta could better convince people to get on board with AI. (Hint: It's green.)

Whatever the plan is, Meta had better figure something out fast. Investors are running out of patience.

Dan DeFrancesco

content_html_zh:
Meta 向投资者传达的信息是：人工智能支出将持续下去，直到回报改善。

投资者的回应：不用了，谢谢。

人工智能支出是 Meta 第二季度收益报告的一大焦点。 而且这种说法也没有足够的说服力来阻止盘后的抛售。

Meta 很高兴地认为 AI 帮助其广告业务（其面包和黄油）增长了 27%。 这不仅仅是纯粹的增长。 广告展示次数增长了 14%，而每个广告的平均价格上涨了 12%。

只有一个问题。 Meta 仍在人工智能投资上花费了令人难以置信的金额——311 亿美元，大约是去年支出的两倍。 这消耗了其自由现金流的很大一部分，从 85.5 亿美元增至 7.84 亿美元。 一位分析师表示，人工智能策略就像“把意大利面条扔到墙上”。

投资者并不为所动，Meta 的股价在盘后一度下跌了近 10%。

与昨天报道的另一家科技巨头微软相比。 它在 Azure 和 Microsoft 365 Copilot 中取得了胜利，微软首席财务官艾米·胡德 (Amy Hood) 在向 BI 的阿什利·斯图尔特 (Ashley Stewart) 查看的员工发布的季度备忘录中对此进行了大力宣传。 也许更重要的是，其人工智能预算预测没有变化。

投资者注意到了。 微软股价在盘后交易中上涨近 8%。

两者之间的区别很明显：人工智能支出很好…… 只要有直接且可衡量的回报。

首席执行官马克扎克伯格阐述了为什么 Meta 的人工智能赌注可能需要更多时间。

人工智能的许多最直接的用例都是针对开发人员的。 看看氛围编码的繁荣就知道了。 扎克伯格在周三的财报电话会议上表示：“为消费者建造有点不同，”但这也是一个“巨大的市场机会”。

还有谁比社交网络之王更适合服务这个市场呢？ Meta 在 Facebook、Instagram、WhatsApp 和 Threads 等平台上拥有数十亿用户。 扎克伯格表示，Meta 在人工智能代理上下了很大的赌注。

所有这些都遵循，但有一个小例外：许多美国人对人工智能感到非常紧张。

Meta 试图通过大力推动人工智能公关来缓解这些担忧，其中包括扎克伯格的专栏文章和一些记者采访。 （与 BI Today 交谈的请求肯定被我的垃圾邮件收件箱捕获了。 我很高兴聊天，马克。 听起来你有一个非常酷的健身房。）

BI 的 Peter Kafka 对于 Meta 如何更好地说服人们接受人工智能有一个想法。 （提示：它是绿色的。）

不管计划是什么，梅塔最好尽快想出办法。 投资者已经失去耐心。
